title: From Subscriptions to Usage-Based Pricing: A Payment Guide for Tech & AI Businesses in Southeast Asia
summary: A guide to payments for Tech and AI businesses in Southeast Asia, from subscriptions to usage-based pricing, with flexible billing and recovery from Xendit. The post From Subscriptions to Usage-Based Pricing: A Payment Guide for Tech & AI Businesses in Southeast Asia appeared first on Xendit .
body_markdown:
Payments for


**Tech and AI businesses** in


**Southeast Asia** are getting harder to standardize, because the way these products charge customers keeps changing.


Subscription payments have long been a dependable model for software companies, letting customers pay on a


**recurring schedule** for continued access to a product or service. That is now changing for Tech and AI businesses, where a fixed recurring charge has become only one of several ways to price a product.


A business might charge for tokens consumed, API calls made, compute used, or prepaid credits purchased, often combining fixed and variable charges in a single plan. As these companies commercialize across the region, their payment setup has to support these


**more flexible ways of charging** without becoming difficult to manage.


A payment setup that fits these models turns more sign-ups into paying customers and keeps them paying as usage grows.


**Here is what this article covers:**


- The four ways Tech and AI businesses in Southeast Asia are pricing their products, from subscriptions to usage-based and hybrid models


- What each pricing model needs from your payment setup, including variable billing, reusable payment credentials, and payment recovery


- How to keep payments reliable for always-on AI products and offer the local payment methods each market uses


- How to scale subscription and usage-based payments across the region without rebuilding for every market


## **How Tech and AI businesses are structuring payments in Southeast Asia**


Southeast Asia's AI sector is scaling fast, and the funding behind it is substantial. Google's


[e-Conomy SEA 2025 report](https://business.google.com/en-all/think/ai-excellence/e-conomy-sea-2025-ai-growth/) counts more than


**680 native AI startups** that drew over


**USD 2.3 billion in investment** in the year to June 2025. For your business, that pace means a large cohort of AI companies will reach commercialization around the same time, so the pricing and payment decisions being made now will shape how the next wave of products earns revenue.


The


**concentration of capital** points the same way. More than


**30%** of


**private funding** in the region over the past 12 months went to


**AI** . When that much capital moves into one category, competition for paying customers gets sharper, and how easily a customer can pay for your product becomes part of whether you win and keep them.


As these products move from launch to monetization, companies are testing different ways of converting usage into revenue.


**Four pricing models** now come up most often among AI products in the region, and each one places a different demand on how you collect payment:


### **1. Subscription-based payments**


Fixed monthly or annual subscriptions still fit AI products that give customers ongoing access to a defined set of features. In Malaysia,


[ILMUchat](https://www.ilmu.ai/#section-roi) , built by YTL AI Labs, runs a free tier alongside a Pro plan at RM50 per month, a straightforward recurring model for consumer AI access.


To support this, your business needs


**scheduled recurring collection** and a dependable way to


**retain a customer's payment credentials** for future billing cycles, so each renewal can be charged without asking the customer to start over.


### **2. Usage-based and pay-as-you-go payments**


For products where usage drives both the cost to run them and the value customers get, the amount you charge can move up or down with how much a customer actually uses. In Vietnam,


[GreenNode](https://greennode.ai/) runs its


**Model-as-a-Service platform** on


**pay-as-you-go pricing** with no fixed monthly fee, so customers pay according to how much of the model they use as they scale.


The payment implication is that


**billing amounts change** from one period to the next, which asks more of your setup than a fixed subscription, since the amount to charge has to be


**calculated** and


**applied correctly** for every cycle.


### **3. Prepaid credits and top-ups**


Another common approach lets customers buy credits upfront and spend them across different AI services. In Thailand,


[iApp Technology](https://iapp.co.th/pricing) uses iApp Credits (IC) as a


**prepaid currency** across its AI APIs, where customers buy credits and consume them on a pay-as-you-go basis, and different APIs deduct different amounts per request. iApp also notes that its credits do not expire, which keeps the balance usable over time.


For your payment flow, this model has to support


**one-time top-up purchases** alongside


**ongoing consumption** of the product.


### **4. Hybrid pricing**


Some AI businesses


**combine recurring access with extra usage purchases** in the same plan. In Malaysia,


[ILMU's developer plans](https://console.ilmu.ai/pricing) pair a monthly per-seat subscription, starting at RM25 per seat, with optional one-time token top-up packs, such as 35 million tokens for RM30. This shows how fixed recurring access and variable consumption can work together inside one monetization model.


The payment setup then has to handle a


**scheduled per-seat charge** and


**irregular top-up purchases** at the same time.


These four models share one requirement. The payment infrastructure supporting them has to bill different amounts, repeat charges without friction, recover payments that fail, and extend across markets, all while staying manageable as complexity grows.


## **What AI businesses need from a flexible payment infrastructure**


As Tech and AI businesses adopt more


**flexible monetization** , their payment infrastructure has to accommodate changing billing amounts, repeat transactions, payment recovery, and regional expansion, without adding operational weight.


These are the


**payment infrastructure capabilities** a Tech or AI business needs to bill flexibly and collect reliably across Southeast Asia, and where Xendit supports each one:


### **1. Flexible billing for variable usage**


Usage-based and hybrid products can charge a different amount every billing cycle, so your infrastructure needs to handle recurring charges that go beyond a fixed monthly fee.


With Xendit,


[Usage-Based Subscriptions](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/usage-based-subscriptions) let you charge a recurring amount based on what each customer consumed, which fits AI APIs, cloud services, storage, data processing, and other consumption-led products. The amount for each cycle is set before that cycle begins through the


[Update Cycle API](https://docs.xendit.co/apidocs/update-subscription-cycle-2) , and Xendit sends a webhook for every upcoming cycle (an automated status message delivered to your systems) so the correct charge is in place before the billing date.


### **2. Different levels of control over billing**


Some businesses want an automated recurring schedule they do not have to manage, while others already run their own metering or billing engine and need to decide exactly when and how much each customer is charged.


With Xendit, you can use


[Xendit Subscriptions](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/how-subscriptions-work) for managed recurring billing, where Xendit handles the scheduling and automatic deductions and you monitor webhooks for each cycle, or you can use Xendit's APIs directly when you need more control over the billing logic and the timing of each transaction. That choice lets your team keep its existing usage calculations in place and use Xendit only for collection.


### **3. Reusable payment methods for repeat charges**


Recurring and usage-based products should not make a customer repeat the whole payment journey every time a new charge occurs.


With Xendit,


[tokenization](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/cards-recurring-and-merchant-initiated-transactions) securely links an eligible payment credential and reuses it for later payments, so customers avoid re-entering details and your business does not store sensitive card data itself.


For a scheduled subscription, the stored credential is held as a recurring card on file. For charges that happen on an as-needed basis, such as a prepaid top-up or a variable usage bill, the same credential can be stored as an unscheduled card on file, known as a


[Merchant-Initiated Transaction](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/cards-recurring-and-merchant-initiated-transactions) , which lets you charge the customer when the need arises instead of on a fixed date. Card details are collected through a Xendit-hosted page, which keeps the card-handling compliance burden off your own systems.


### **4. A recovery path when recurring payments fail**


A failed renewal or usage charge does not always mean the customer wants to stop using the product, so your business needs a way to recover a temporary failure before it becomes lost revenue.


With Xendit, you can


[configure recovery options](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/recover-failed-payments) for a subscription plan, including attaching up to five


[payment channels](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/available-payment-channels) in a priority order so a declined charge moves automatically to the next method, automatic retries timed to when customers tend to top up their funds, and a


[one-time Payment Link](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/payment-1) that lets the customer settle a specific cycle using any method, even one not attached to the plan. Each attempt reports back through webhooks, so your records stay current without manual checking.


### **5. Reliable payments for always-on digital products**


AI and digital products can be used at any hour, so a customer might subscribe, upgrade, or top up at any time, and


**payment downtime can interrupt monetization** at the exact moment someone intends to pay.


**Since 2025, Xendit maintains**[99.999% uptime](https://www.xendit.co/en-id/blog/xendit-payment-reliability-99-999-uptime/) across its overall API and webhook traffic, which works out to around five minutes of downtime per year at that level of availability. For an always-on product, that


**reliability protects revenue** during the off-peak hours and sudden spikes when a customer is ready to pay and your team is not watching.


### **Local payment flexibility across Southeast Asia**


A Tech or AI product can run the same monetization model everywhere, but how customers prefer to pay differs across Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Indonesia.


With Xendit, your business can reach


[100+ payment methods](https://www.xendit.co/en/products/all-payment-methods/) across its supported markets through one payment infrastructure, so you can add locally relevant options without rebuilding your core billing for each new country. That coverage matters in a region where payment preferences shift sharply between neighboring markets, and many customers keep their money in e-wallets and bank accounts they use more often than cards.


******


Once these pieces are in place and the monetization model works, the next task is extending it to more customers and markets without multiplying the work behind it.

## **How to scale subscription and usage-based payments across Southeast Asia with Xendit**


The capabilities above make each billing model work. Scaling means running them across more customers, markets, and pricing models without the payment setup growing more complex each time.


These are the practices


**Xendit supports** to scale subscription and usage-based payments across Southeast Asia:


**1. Keep the billing logic at the product level**


Your subscription, usage calculation, or hybrid pricing logic can stay consistent inside the product, while the payment layer absorbs the differences between local markets. That leaves one set of billing rules to maintain instead of one per country.


**2. Add local payment methods as a configuration step**


Entering Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines, Singapore, or Indonesia should not require a separate billing architecture for each country simply because customers pay in different ways. Adding a market becomes a setup decision, so your engineering team keeps building the product instead of rebuilding payments.


**3. Hold visibility as transaction volume climbs**


As more recurring and variable charges run through the system, your finance and operations teams need consistent transaction status, reporting, and reconciliation data across markets, instead of separate records to stitch together for each one.


**4. Let the payment setup change with the product**


A Tech or AI business may move from free trials to subscriptions, add usage-based plans, introduce prepaid credits, or combine several pricing models as it matures. Your payment infrastructure should support those shifts without a full rebuild each time the model changes.


Handled this way, expansion becomes a series of configuration decisions instead of repeated engineering projects.

## **Let payments evolve with your product**


Tech and AI products can change fast, and how they make money often changes with them. A payment layer that only handles a flat monthly charge will hold the product back the moment you introduce usage-based pricing, prepaid credits, or a hybrid plan. Xendit supports recurring and usage-based payments, gives you the choice between managed billing and direct API control, keeps payment credentials reusable for repeat charges, recovers failed payments, and offers local payment methods across Southeast Asia, so the payment layer has room to grow alongside the product.

## **FAQ for Tech and AI businesses in Southeast Asia: Subscription and usage-based payments**


### **How do you bill customers for usage that changes every billing cycle?**


You set the amount for each cycle before it begins, so the charge matches what the customer actually used. With


**Xendit's**[usage-based subscriptions](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/usage-based-subscriptions) , you define the total for each upcoming cycle through the


[Update Cycle API](https://docs.xendit.co/apidocs/update-subscription-cycle-2) before the billing date, and Xendit notifies you of each new cycle by webhook so the correct amount is ready in time. This fits AI APIs, compute, and storage products where the bill is different every period.


### **Can an AI business charge for prepaid credits and top-ups through the same setup as its subscriptions?**


Yes. Prepaid credit purchases are one-time charges, and they can run alongside recurring plans on the same payment infrastructure. With


**Xendit** , you can store a customer's payment credential as an unscheduled card on file, a


[Merchant-Initiated Transaction](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/cards-recurring-and-merchant-initiated-transactions) , and charge it when a customer tops up or when a variable usage bill is due, while a separate recurring plan handles any fixed subscription. That lets a hybrid product collect both types of payment without a second integration.


### **What happens when a recurring or usage-based payment fails?**


A failed charge does not have to end the subscription when there is a


[recovery path](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/recover-failed-payments) behind it.


**Xendit** lets you attach up to five payment channels to a plan in a priority order, retry failed charges automatically, and send the customer a one-time


[Payment Link](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/creating-payment-links) to complete a specific cycle with any method. You receive webhook updates on each attempt, so your team can see which renewals recovered and which need attention.


### **Can you keep your own metering or billing engine and still use Xendit to collect payment?**


Yes. Some Tech and AI businesses already calculate usage themselves and only need a reliable way to charge for it. With


**Xendit** , you can use the


[Payments API](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/how-payments-api-work) directly to control when each transaction is created and how much to charge, while still using tokenized credentials and payment recovery, so your existing metering logic stays in place and Xendit handles collection.


### **Do customers have to re-enter their card for every repeat charge?**


No. Making customers repeat the full payment flow for every charge adds friction and lowers completion.


**Xendit** uses tokenization to securely link an eligible payment credential once and


[reuse it for later recurring](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/reusable-payment-codes) or


[usage-based charges](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/usage-based-subscriptions) , and card details are collected on a Xendit-hosted page so your business does not store the card data itself.


### **Which payment methods should an AI product accept across Southeast Asia?**


Start with the methods customers in each market already use, which across much of the region means e-wallets and bank-based transfers alongside cards.


**Xendit** gives your business access to


[local payment methods](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/available-payment-channels) across its supported markets through one integration, so you can offer the options each country prefers without building a separate setup for every market. Matching local preferences supports both sign-up and renewal, since customers commit more easily to a method they already trust.
